context:
Goal: a Reset on the phone never destroys check-ins that can't be got back.
Problem (cannot undo): when the saved-version copy can't be written, the web still runs Reset and shows a banner saying it can't be undone. The native app refuses the Reset. They differ, and only you can say which is right.
Based on (read): debt native-milestone-needed-unpinned.
Based on (read): decision unwritable-store-says-so.
Departs from: src/app.jsx:resetAll — the web goes ahead with a banner; option a keeps the phone refusing the Reset instead.
Meanwhile: pins works on its other debts. Nothing waits on this.
home: decision milestones-taken-before-risk (branch pin-reset-milestone 6c65379, landing at merge)

options.gain: A Reset can never wipe check-ins that have no saved copy.
options.how: With no saved copy, the phone says the Reset can't run and changes nothing.
options.label: Keep the phone refusing
options.lose: On a full or broken store, Reset doesn't work until the store is fixed.

options.gain: Both apps act the same, and Reset always works.
options.how: The phone runs the Reset and shows the web's can't-be-undone banner.
options.label: Match the web: Reset runs with the banner
options.lose: One tap can destroy months of check-ins with no way back.

ref: debt native-milestone-needed-unpinned (the saved-copy rule before a Reset is unpinned); decision unwritable-store-says-so (an unwritable store says so)
title: When the saved copy can't be written, should a Reset on the phone still run?
why: It keeps the one act that can't be undone behind its safety copy.
